description: A file name or path printed in a terminal is a link when it exists: absolute paths, ~ paths, paths relative to the folder the terminal is in, and bare file names, with or without a :line suffix. Hover it and it underlines; Cmd-click it on a Mac (Ctrl-click elsewhere, a tap on a phone) and a small menu opens at the pointer. A file offers open in carnivore (the default, so Enter picks it), open in browser and show in finder. A folder offers open in carnivore, which shows the files browser, and show in finder. The browser and Finder open on the computer the session runs on. On a phone only open in carnivore shows. A paired computer's terminal links no paths.
examples: A test fails at src/app.py:42: Cmd-click it and open it in Carnivore's file viewer.
git status lists a changed file: Cmd-click it and pick show in finder.
ls prints index.html: Cmd-click it and open it in your browser.
how_to: Move the pointer over a file name or path in a terminal: it underlines when the file exists.
Hold Cmd (Ctrl on Windows or Linux) and click it. Pick open in carnivore, open in browser or show in finder.
On a touch screen, tap the path and pick open in carnivore.
media_exempt: a hover underline and a pointer menu are not visible in a still capture; recaptured at the version bump
